[b]____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________[/b]

[b]Business News[/b]

[b]To connect the World[/b]

ESPN has come to an agreement with the professional football league of Valderra, known as the Lagonda Supaliga for sponsorship reasons, to become an official broadcaster of the season for the next foreseeable future. The Supaliga season runs from September  February and will allow fans of Bascovers own professional league, the ARC Energy Professional Football League Men, will be able to watch these earlier games before tuning into the A League.

BBC has continued to cement itself as the premier global broadcasting service as it expands its operations to Daesun, Vespurias, the Neue Republik, Valderra, and all nations within the Belorev region. The BBC will offer its news, weather, documentary, business, and music for regional services.

[b]Holiday destination: The World[/b]

Aurora Airlines has announced the addition of four new destinations in the country of Valderra, making it the fifth nation to be served by Aurora. Aurora Airlines offers tickets to and from the cities Vald, Therene, Serene City, and Bandar Samir. 

The partnership between Aurora and Valderra continues to strengthen after a BC$9.83 million ($7.2 million) deal sees Aurora become the primary sponsor of the domestic cup of the Valderran Lagonda Supaliga.

[b]Sports news[/b]

[b]Jets soar to 3[/b]

Game 4 of the Major Hockey League Howe Cup playoffs have come to an end with another victory for the Duncan Jets, beating the Sinunimak Krakens 32 in a shootout. The victors bested their opponents at their own home, in Climate Pledge Arena, Sinunimak. From the get-go the game was dominated by the Jets, with the Jets having 40 SOG opposed to the Krakens 29, though the Krakens had the upper hand in physicality with 18 hits to the Jets 13. Despite some poor plays and lazy discipline as Jet players spent 8 minutes in the penalty box while the Krakens were only subjected to 6 minutes, the Jets were able to get on the scoreboard first with Blake Wheeler (26) scoring at the 7-minute mark into the second period with an assist from Nikolaj Ehlers (27). 

For the full 12 minutes of the second period, the Krakens ran circles around the Jets. First, John Hayden (15) scored in the 13th minute with an assist from Morgan Geekie (67) and Jamie Oleksiak (24). Then, 6 minutes later, Jared McCann (19) brought the Krakens to a 2-1 lead following a goal in the 19th minute complimented by assists from Vince Dunn (29) and Eeli Tolvanen (20). Fortunately for the Jets, Peter Louis (80) was able to tie the game 9 minutes into the third period with the help of teammates Josh Morrissey (44) and Kyle Connor (81). The game was forced into overtime, which remained scoreless, and it wasnt until the Fifth round when Mark Scheifele scored to win it for the Jets.

The teams travel back to the Bascover Life Centre in Duncan, Qanuingittuq, on 19 February. The game is a do-or-die game for both teams, as Jets just need one more win to claim the Howe Cup for the ninth time in the clubs history.

[b]Argos Sport Initiative[/b]

CEO of the governing body of Rugby Union in Bascover, C.J. Pestonji, has invited the Rugby Union associations of New Westmore, USO, ULR, Nordiheim, South Argos, the Valonian States, Tranvalia, Eregovia, Ascoiya, and the New Balion Empire to come together and a men's professional rugby union club competition known as Super Rugby Argos that will host at least 2 teams from across all participating countries.  Further details regarding the competitions layout will be revealed once the respective invited associations get back to Bascover Rugby Union.

[b]Closer to the Cup[/b]

The 2026 FEFA World Cup is the first World Cup that Bascover has ever qualified for and has proven itself with a Round 1 Win in the Group Stages. Placed in Group D alongside Wuloosya, Maqamistan, and the Tianyou Dynasty, the Bascover Blues have won their first game against Wuloosya.

The game started off with the Blues pushing offensively, forcing Wuloosya to be on the defensive early on. Unfortunately for the Wuloosyan team, the constant pressure from the Blues was too much, as striker Jonathan David (who currently plays in the A-League for Courtenay Mariners) was able to score from a tight angle in the box at the 19th minute mark. The Blues would elect to remain on the defensive for the rest of the game, focusing on minimising the possession of Wuloosya and passing the ball amongst themselves at the back till the full-time whistle, ending the game 11.

The Blues now face the Tianyou Dynasty, who won their first game against Maqamistan 21. A win for either team would almost certainly guarantee qualification for the Round of 16 stage.

[b]Parliament discusses policies to reform the administrative system.
[sub]Le Parlement débat des politiques de réforme du système administratif.[/b][/sub]
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────[/list]

[i][b]P A R L I A M E N T / P A R L E M E N T ─[/b][/i] Recently, on February 13, at the [b]Pirn Parliament[/b], an independent senator, [i][b]Aglaë Fèvre[/b][/i], raised an issue concerning Pirns current administrative system. According to Fèvre, the existing [b]Four-Level [/b]administrative mechanism, consisting of [i]Provincial Level, District Level, Communal Level, and Hamlet Level[/i], is overly cumbersome, complicated, slow, and no longer suitable for Pirns current social, economic, and political conditions.

She provided examples such as citizens complaining that land-grant procedures for building houses take far too long, three, sometimes even five months, and in some cases up to a year, because after submitting an application at the Hamlet Level, it must be transferred to the Commune, then to the District, before finally reaching the Province, even though the District functions merely as a middleman. Regarding the registration of permanent residence, many people jokingly say: [i][b]When we first got married, we submitted the permanent residence registration at the Hamlet. By the time it was approved, we already had a grandchild.[/b][/i] Although exaggerated, the joke reflects how passing documents through too many levels creates unnecessarily long delays, even when citizens urgently need those papers to function normally. Many local and foreign businesses also complain about the long waiting times for approval and the excessive paperwork, commitments, etc., which significantly hinder economic development in many localities.

She then proposed abolishing the District Level and replacing the four-tier system with a three-tier one, [i]Provincial, Communal, and Hamlet[/i], which is widely used in many countries, aiming to streamline the bureaucracy and make it smoother, less cumbersome, and less complex.

Once Fèvres proposal was presented, the Parliament grew lively, not only because some members opposed it, but also because the issue itself is complex. Since Pirn gained independence in 1955, the administrative division system has remained unchanged, meaning that reorganizing it would be one of the greatest reforms ever undertaken in the country. Despite objections from certain influential party members, most supported her concerns, and the proposal was approved by the Parliament and placed under [b]Top Priority Proposals[/b] for review. According to [b][i]Randall Dawson[/i][/b], one of the opposing parliamentarians:

▍[i]Such reform would create great complications. If this proposal is brought forward at the next convention in September and passes, everything will be chaotic. First is the merging of Provinces, Communes, and Hamlets after the District Level is dissolved. This will require reallocating district-level officials appropriately, for example, promoting those with sufficient competence to the Province or Commune Level. But, as I said, this is extremely complex because it requires accurately assessing their abilities. Second, many citizens, especially the elderly and the youth, may feel a loss of local identity after the mergers. There will surely be demands for new names. For instance, if Commune A merges with Commune B, many will insist the new name be C instead of A or B. The same applies to Hamlets and Provinces, if we reuse an old name, people from the other area will feel their identity and hometown have been erased. The problem wasn't just coming up with new names, but also deciding which hamlets should be merged with which, which communes should be merged with which, and which provinces should be merged with which, because many developing areas suddenly had to shoulder the problems of other areas after the merger.[/i]

Nevertheless, many of the opposing members also expressed a shared sentiment that the current four-level system is indeed overly complex. Even though the Parliament has passed many laws aiming to simplify administrative procedures for citizens, numerous lawmakers and experts believe that most of these reforms lack long-term sustainability and only remain effective for 2-4 years.

▍[i]I believe Dawsons viewpoint is partly correct,[/i] said [b][i]Greg Ortega[/i][/b], a member of the [b]Future Vision Party[/b]. [i]But that difficulty is only temporary. Yes, people will initially feel they are losing their local identity and sense of home. Yes, reallocating district officials based on their abilities will be complicated. Yes, citizens, especially those in former Provinces, Communes, and Hamlets, will have to reapply for new documents. But all of this is temporary. We will gradually adapt, and things will run more smoothly. Its like watering a plant, you cannot expect it to grow fully by tomorrow. And clearly, if we maintain the current four-level system, the problem will worsen like a malignant tumor spreading, and citizens will suffer more. Thomas Lavery, the father of our nation, once said that the government is the loyal servant of the people and must ensure their greatest comfort.[/i] Ortega stated.

At present, it remains uncertain whether Fèvres proposal will undergo in-depth discussion at the next parliamentary meeting. However, based on her remarks, the issue of administrative division has once again become a heated topic among both citizens and authorities.
